title: ezdxf binary proxy-graphic fix and artifact boundary

sources.name: Autodesk ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY DXF reference
sources.observed: Defines group 92 as graphics byte size, group 310 as binary graphics chunks, group 93 as entity-data bit size, and a separate optional group-310 entity-data sequence.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Field-role contract only; not arbitrary proxy validity, semantic execution safety, or 3D interpretation.

sources.name: Autodesk common entity group codes
sources.observed: Describes group 92 as the byte count for subsequent group-310 proxy-graphics chunks and cautions that displayed code-table ordering is not immutable.
sources.evidenceCeiling: DXF field description; not a universal ordering rule or native acceptance result.

sources.name: ezdxf issue #1412
sources.observed: ezdxf 1.4.4 ASCII proxy-graphic output succeeded while Binary DXF output raised TypeError because a pre-encoded string was passed to a binary writer expecting bytes.
sources.revision: Issue opened 2026-08-29; closed as completed by PR #1418 on 2026-10-02.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Issue report for the named version/runtime; not a libdxfrw defect.

sources.name: ezdxf PR #1418 merge commit
sources.observed: Merged change passes raw DXFBinaryTag chunks through the tag-writer protocol and adds generated ASCII/Binary payload tests across AC1021/AC1024 count-code profiles and size boundaries.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Merged-source behavior and its added regression shape; no peer artifact was executed in this review.

sources.name: ezdxf v1.4.5 release tag
sources.observed: The public release page identifies v1.4.5 and target commit 84ae319.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Release source identity only; this pass did not establish that the tag contains c87c87e or inspect the release tree.

sources.name: PyPI ezdxf release metadata
sources.observed: PyPI lists upload date 2026-10-16, sdist SHA-256 a6c3bbc1a65ce764d97c5beafe6ae693d8ed14c6cdae366b50e1974a79d4a00, and pure-Python wheel SHA-256 70a79ec7d40990f60453e3c87ffe9f668907ee061cf6f4c0a3794d032ec2b40e.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Artifact identity/checksum metadata, not source-to-artifact binding or runtime behavior.

sources.name: Local libdxfrw output and tests
sources.observed: The writer emits version-dependent count codes 92/160 and group-310 chunks from the raw byte carrier. The exact 0/127/128/255/256-byte chunk-boundary matrix is LINE-based; current replay admission also allows POINT, CIRCLE, ARC, and ELLIPSE, for which the existing test owner contains generated positive routes. The source/test inventory supersedes older plan text describing a LINE-only allowlist.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Local raw-carrier transport regression scope; not arbitrary proxy semantics, ACIS/ACDS, B-rep, or native application qualification.

conclusions: The stale instruction to re-resolve ezdxf PR #1418 is superseded: the issue is closed by merged source commit c87c87e65937feede396e5861eec703bde701ec8.
The v1.4.5 release tag and PyPI checksums identify candidate artifacts but were not bound to the merged fix or executed; package-level comparator status remains unqualified.
Local PAR-76/PAR-128 coverage already tests the relevant binary-carrier encoding boundary, so no new local test, code, fixture, dependency, or CTest is justified.
This work is non-promoting: findings/subplans remain 141/78 and J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain DEFERRED_EXTERNAL.
actions: At the next already-planned composed comparator checkpoint, pin one exact ezdxf artifact hash and verify ASCII and Binary proxy chunk equality, byte counts, and next-record alignment before recording comparator success.
Do not block local implementation or per-slice fast validation on optional ezdxf availability.
